newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian gold stocks achieve late-year boom.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian gold stocks achieve late-year boom.

text.p: Australian gold stocks have taken on a late-year shine due to takeover speculation and hopes that small explorers have discovered a major new gold province in South Australia's Gawler Craton.

Takeovers are being tipped for a number of companies, ranging from the troubled Newcrest Mining Ltd, following its illfated move earlier this year on Normandy Mining Ltd, to Wiluna Mines Ltd, Acacia Ltd and Australian Resources Ltd.

Analysts say moves could come from within Australia but the bets are on North American companies, where the taste for growth has been recently seen in the competing bids by Newmont Mining Corp and Homestake Mining Co for Sante Fe Pacific Gold Corp.

"The bottom line is Australian stocks are very undervalued relative to their North American cousins," Kevin Kartun, gold analyst with BZW Australia told Reuters, saying the offshore stocks carry a strong exploration upside currently lacking here.

The year began nicely for producers with the spike in the gold price, which prompted a number to reduce their forward selling positions, but investors became disillusioned as the price dropped, and sentiment has been adverse toward the end of 1996 when the gold market seasonally is strong, Kartun said.
Affecting the price are rumours of gold sales by the International Monetary Fund and central European banks, and bearish views by the World Gold Council on demand.

The gold price fell to US$368.90 (A$465.84) an ounce on Wednesday from US$386.85 (A$521.01) at the end of 1995 and the massive February 2 high of US$417.17 (A$550.79), the rising Australian dollar hitting local producers with a double whammy.

"You have seen the Australian dollar gold price at four year lows, and people who are unhedged would be facing the full blast of that, a number of their operations would be looking quite sorry," Kartun said.
The Australian gold index fell to 1784.7 points on Wednesday from 1862.0 points a year ago, a drop understating the fall from the year high of 2287.7 during the February gold high.
Kartun believes overseas investors, who are aggressive for growth, have been put off the Australian market by a lack of major exploration success, as well as some management concerns.

But he sees improvements in the September quarterly reports and the focus on the Gawler Craton which saw the share price of premier stock Helix Resources NL rise to A$4.15 from 37 cents, pushing its market value from A$15.6 million to A$175 million.

The A$400 million takeover move by Canada's Placer Dome Inc on Highlands Gold Ltd and A$310 million scrip offer for local offshoot Placer Pacific has led to speculation as to who is next, pushing up the share price of the unhedged Newcrest.
While Bell Securities' analyst Keith Goode sees Australian gold production gradually rising overall over the next 12 months, he says the market has lost some interest in the major producers.

"The market goes into phases and currently we seem to be in an exploration phase....because there are so many stocks involved in that end, it will probably last for a bit," he said, adding some North American investors, who he would not name, were taking up exploration positions across a broad base.

Garry Duncan from ABN Amro Hoare Govett said he is a firm believer in the potential of the Craton, a 350,000 square kilometre under-explored region with little outcrop which has been opened up by aeromagnetic surveys and calcrete sampling.
"It has the potential to host massive deposits," he said.
"People think it is a short term rally but I think it has got a long way to go," he said.

Duncan said ABN Amro currently views the gold index as underweight to the all ordinaries index, the key share market barometer. He said the brokerage firm is focused on growth and defensive stocks which have a good hedging policy, among them Lihir, Great Central, Normandy and Sons of Gwalia.
"We are bullish on stocks, we are not particularly bullish on price," he said.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
